definition: Ultimatum means a final demand that carries a threat if it is refused.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ultimatum. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ultimatum should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The drummer's ultimatum reached the band by text: hire a real sound engineer before the tour bus leaves, or the drum kit rides home with me.
A request is far gentler than an ultimatum — it asks, and takes no for an answer.
A demand is milder than an ultimatum — it insists, but an ultimatum adds the clock and the consequence: do this by then, or else.

A threat is a promised harm — do nothing, and it may still land. An ultimatum wraps a threat around a final choice: meet the stated demand by the stated deadline, or the harm follows. The threat is only the or-else; the ultimatum is the whole locked package of terms.

A warning cautions that something bad may happen, and it can stand alone — no terms attached, nothing asked of you at all. An ultimatum always asks: it bundles a demand, a deadline, and a stated consequence into one final package. Every ultimatum warns; very few warnings are ultimatums.
